title: Worker Task
description: A bounded unit of work that OpenClaw delegates to a worker (Claude, Codex, or another adapter). Worker tasks are the only way bounded execution crosses the trust boundary from control plane to worker.

kind.description: Task category. 'debug' added in M5.1 to absorb agent-worker.mjs's 'debug' mode; semantically close to 'code-review' + 'research' but distinct in operator intent (root-cause investigation).

trust_level.description: Resolved at enqueue time against trust-policy.schema.json. Workers MUST refuse if their actions exceed this level.

status.description: Task lifecycle state. Matches the directory names under ~/.cache/agent-continuity/queue/{state}/. 'running' is entered when a worker (e.g. agent-worker.mjs) actively executes a claimed task; M5.3 will add the worker.sh start subcommand that drives claimed → running. Until then no path in this codebase transitions to running, but submit accepts it as a valid from-state so .mjs can move tasks through.

context_refs.description: Pointers into the shared memory (context.md / decisions.md anchors).

files_allowed.description: Glob patterns. Worker refuses to write outside this set.

permissions.description: Per-task execution permissions, preserved verbatim from agent-worker.mjs's task shape (M5.1). NOT interpreted by this layer's trust-policy resolver — those checks remain on trust_level and the policy-side files_denied/allow_kinds/etc. This block exists so .mjs's tasks round-trip through this layer's queue without data loss. dangerous_bypass and network=on are refused by .mjs at execution time; this layer additionally constrains them at the schema level (network is enum-locked to 'off', dangerous_bypass is allowed as a field but workers must refuse to act on true).

expected_artifacts.description: What the worker should produce. Used at result time to verify completeness.

process.description: Subprocess execution metadata, set by runners (e.g. agent-worker.mjs runTask) at submit time via worker.sh submit --process-info. Optional. Provides timing, exit code, timeout flag, and log path so the canonical task record carries enough to debug a failed run without consulting runner-side ephemera. Added in M5.3c after the M5.3b bridge surfaced that .mjs's process info was being dropped between subprocess completion and the queue.

code.description: Process exit code; null if signal-killed before exit

signal.description: Signal that terminated the process (e.g. SIGTERM, SIGKILL); null if exited cleanly

timed_out.description: True if the runner enforced timeout (SIGTERM → SIGKILL)

log.description: Absolute path to the runner's log file

audit.description: Append-only trail of state transitions and any tool calls the worker made.
